# AetherEdge

> Complete agent index for the deterministic AetherIoT edge runtime, Kernel, CLI, SDK, contracts, and implementation references.

Default to read-only. Static documentation does not grant execution authority. Before any write, load the safety policy and query the live application capability catalog. Never automatically retry a command whose outcome is unknown, timed out, or missing audit evidence. AetherEdge retains final authority over physical execution.

Use the narrowest document that answers the task. The catalog covers every agent-readable Edge document; deep implementation records remain available under Optional.

- [Machine-readable document catalog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/EvanL1/AetherEdge/main/ai/docs-manifest.json)
- [Document catalog schema](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/EvanL1/AetherEdge/main/ai/docs-manifest.schema.json)

## Agent Task Manual

- [Add a data processor](https://github.com/EvanL1/AetherEdge/blob/main/ai/runbooks/add-data-processor.md): Read the authoritative AetherEdge resource at ai/runbooks/add-data-processor.md.
- [Build a downstream integration](https://github.com/EvanL1/AetherEdge/blob/main/ai/runbooks/build-downstream-integration.md): Read the authoritative AetherEdge resource at ai/runbooks/build-downstream-integration.md.
- [Change an AI-facing capability](https://github.com/EvanL1/AetherEdge/blob/main/ai/runbooks/change-capability.md): Read the authoritative AetherEdge resource at ai/runbooks/change-capability.md.
- [Connect AI Assistants](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/guides/ai-assistants.md): Point Claude or any MCP client at aether mcp, and choose between read-only and write access
- [Build Applications with AI](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/guides/build-applications-with-ai.md): Generate contract-first IoT applications without turning a Web UI or an AI agent into a second runtime authority
- [Connect Devices](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/guides/connect-devices.md): Commission protocol channels, inspect exact runtime availability, and map physical points to device instances
- [Connect Data Processors](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/guides/data-processors.md): Declare data-processing tasks in domain packs and connect request-driven local or remote processors
- [Connect AetherEdge to AetherCloud through AetherContracts](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/guides/edge-contracts-cloud.md): This agent task validates the current cross-repository integration path without claiming production CloudLink readiness. It starts with a safe local runtime, verifies the shared contract release, and then runs the available product…
- [Getting Started](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/guides/getting-started.md): Install a safe-empty runtime, establish operator access, verify health, and choose the next commissioning step
- [Writing Rules](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/guides/writing-rules.md): Author rules through the HTTP API or a downstream product console
- [AetherEdge](https://github.com/EvanL1/AetherEdge/blob/main/skills/aether-iot/SKILL.md): Build, integrate, diagnose, or generate applications for the AetherEdge AI-native edge kernel. Use for AetherEdge onboarding, SDK compositions, device and topology clients, read-only operations UIs, MCP integration, Domain Packs, or governed IoT commands where live-state authority and physical-device safety must be preserved.

## Deployment and Operations

- [Deployment](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/guides/deployment.md): Run with Docker Compose or build a self-contained installer for edge devices
- [Home Assistant integration extraction](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/migration/home-assistant-extraction.md): Migrate installations away from the retired in-kernel Home Assistant bridge
- [Deployment topologies](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/overview/deployment-topologies.md): AetherIoT supports deployments that keep physical authority at the edge while adding cloud coordination only where it creates value.
- [Configuration Reference](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/reference/configuration.md): YAML configuration schema, protocol channel authority, the sync pipeline, and environment variables

## Safety and Governance

- [AetherEdge Agent Instructions](https://github.com/EvanL1/AetherEdge/blob/main/AGENTS.md): This file is the canonical instruction source for coding agents working in this repository. CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md are symlinks to it, so every agent reads and edits the same content. Any further tool-specific file may add usage notes,…
- [Aether invariants](https://github.com/EvanL1/AetherEdge/blob/main/ai/invariants.md): These rules are more important than the current directory layout.
- [safety-policy.yaml](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/EvanL1/AetherEdge/main/ai/safety-policy.yaml): Machine-readable AetherEdge safety-policy.yaml resource.
- [Safe Operations for Applications and Agents](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/guides/safe-operations.md): Preserve identity, confirmation, audit, topology fencing, and uncertain command outcomes when operating AetherEdge
- [Dependency security exceptions](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/security/dependency-exceptions.md): Security advisories are denied by default. An exception is permitted only when the affected operation is unreachable, the boundary is enforced in code and a removal condition is recorded here.

## Recovery

- [CloudLink spool recovery](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/recovery/cloudlink-spool-recovery.md): Recover a file-backed CloudLink spool without discarding unacknowledged facts or fabricating delivery evidence.
- [Configuration rollback and reconciliation](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/recovery/configuration-rollback.md): Recover a commissioned Edge configuration without creating a second authority or repeating an uncertain mutation.
- [Gateway identity recovery](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/recovery/gateway-identity-recovery.md): Contain a lost or compromised Gateway credential and re-establish an experimental CloudLink session without weakening Edge authority.
- [Safe stop and control revocation](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/recovery/safe-stop-and-control-revocation.md): Contain an unsafe or uncertain control path while preserving deterministic local safety and audit evidence.

## Platform Reference

- [catalog.yaml](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/EvanL1/AetherEdge/main/ai/catalog.yaml): Machine-readable AetherEdge catalog.yaml resource.
- [data-processing.yaml](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/EvanL1/AetherEdge/main/ai/evals/data-processing.yaml): Machine-readable AetherEdge data-processing.yaml resource.
- [AI evaluations](https://github.com/EvanL1/AetherEdge/blob/main/ai/evals/README.md): AI evaluations are scenario fixtures that verify capability discovery, authorization, confirmation, audit, and failure behavior. They complement Rust unit tests; they do not replace deterministic runtime tests.
- [AI-native assets](https://github.com/EvanL1/AetherEdge/blob/main/ai/README.md): This directory contains vendor-neutral assets used by coding agents and by AI operators of an Aether gateway.
- [Aether Architecture](https://github.com/EvanL1/AetherEdge/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md): Aether is an AI-native, industry-neutral edge kernel. The target architecture and its boundaries are defined in:
- [AetherCloud](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/aethercloud.md): AetherCloud is the AI-native, industry-neutral, multi-cloud IoT fusion and control plane for AetherEdge runtimes and cloud-side workloads. It is a separate product, not a hosted copy of the edge runtime.
- [AetherContracts](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/aethercontracts.md): AetherContracts is the public, language-neutral interoperability authority for AetherEdge, AetherCloud, and independent implementations.
- [AetherEdge](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/aetheredge.md): AetherEdge is the open-source, industry-neutral Linux edge runtime, Kernel, CLI, and Rust SDK in the AetherIoT product family.
- [Target repository layout](https://github.com/EvanL1/AetherEdge/blob/main/docs/architecture/target-layout.md): The repository is the smallest industry-neutral AetherEdge kernel. Stable contracts, shared kernel implementation, six process owners, and tooling have separate roots. Optional third-party implementations live downstream rather than in an…
- [System Architecture](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/concepts/architecture.md): Isolated edge services communicating over shared memory, per-consumer UDS events, SQLite, HTTP, and MQTT
- [Data Flow](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/concepts/data-flow.md): SHM-native uplink and downlink paths end to end, with latency budgets
- [Data Model](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/concepts/data-model.md): Products, instances, and T/S/C/A points - and why an instance is a pure thing-model with no status field
- [Data Processing Flow](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/concepts/data-processing-flow.md): How Aether assembles governed IoT data, invokes a request-driven processor, validates derived data, and keeps control separate
- [Aether Data Processing](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/concepts/data-processing.md): Industry-neutral, request-driven processing of governed IoT data into validated derived data
- [Rule Engine](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/concepts/rule-engine.md): Dual-column rule storage, tick and event scheduling, execution, and hot reload
- [Shared Memory](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/concepts/shared-memory.md): The SHM data plane - slot layout, writer ownership, seqlock reads, generations, and the PointWatch event plane
- [AI-native platform](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/overview/ai-native-platform.md): AetherIoT is building an open runtime platform for agents to turn human intent into governed, verifiable behavior across physical spaces.
- [AetherIoT platform overview](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/overview/platform.md): AetherIoT is the open-source, AI-native project identity for a family of interoperable products that turn human intent into governed, verifiable behavior across physical spaces. It is not a fourth runtime and does not own a separate wire…
- [AetherEdge User Journeys](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/overview/user-journeys.md): Choose the right product and follow the safe path from an empty edge runtime to a commissioned application
- [Repository documentation map](https://github.com/EvanL1/AetherEdge/blob/main/docs/README.md): Navigation for repository documentation, current authority records, and release support information.
- [CLI Reference](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/reference/cli.md): Every aether command, including services, protocol channels, COMTRADE inspection, sync, doctor, and rules
- [CloudLink MQTT contract](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/reference/cloudlink-mqtt.md): CloudLink has one AetherEdge wire contract. There is no migration mode, protocol negotiation, fallback topic tree, or alternate schema alias.
- [Data Processing Contracts](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/reference/data-processing-contracts.md): Contracts for processing frames, requests, derived results, validation, and failure semantics
- [AetherCloud Gateway enrollment](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/reference/gateway-enrollment.md): Generate and claim a local AetherEdge Gateway identity without implying an active CloudLink credential or session.
- [HTTP API](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/reference/http-api.md): The single remote gateway, service-local OpenAPI, authentication, and canonical path conventions
- [MCP Tools Reference](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/reference/mcp-tools.md): All MCP tools grouped by domain, with parameters and write-safety markers
- [Protocol Adapter Reference](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/reference/protocol-adapters.md): Exact AetherEdge IO feature gates, runtime protocol IDs, transport roles, point mappings, security boundaries, and implemented protocol slices
- [AetherEdge](https://github.com/EvanL1/AetherEdge/blob/main/README.md): Repository overview, current product status, installation paths, architecture boundaries, and development entry points.

## Compatibility and Status

- [Product version compatibility](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/compatibility/version-matrix.md): This matrix distinguishes released compatibility evidence from planned product combinations. A green local test never upgrades an experimental public contract to production status.
- [Platform status and roadmap](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/roadmap/status.md): Status is reported separately for implemented, experimental, and planned capabilities. Product names do not upgrade technical readiness.

## Optional

- [CloudLink v1 alpha 1](https://github.com/EvanL1/AetherEdge/blob/main/contracts/aether-contracts/v0.1.0-alpha.3/spec/cloudlink-v1alpha1.md): AetherContracts is the sole interoperability authority for this protocol slice. Product-repository wire profiles, manifests, gates, and evidence files are non-authoritative implementation overlays and may not add or redefine wire fields.…
- [Consumer distribution v1 alpha 1](https://github.com/EvanL1/AetherEdge/blob/main/contracts/aether-contracts/v0.1.0-alpha.3/spec/distribution-v1alpha1.md): This profile lets AetherCloud, AetherIot, and independent implementations pin one exact AetherContracts release while keeping their default verification path offline. Distribution conformance proves release identity and byte integrity; it…
- [Language-neutral TCK v1 alpha 1](https://github.com/EvanL1/AetherEdge/blob/main/contracts/aether-contracts/v0.1.0-alpha.3/spec/tck-v1alpha1.md): Repository tests compile every normative JSON Schema, validate valid and wire-invalid fixtures, preserve context-invalid distinctions, and verify every declared SHA-256.
- [CloudLink contracts](https://github.com/EvanL1/AetherEdge/blob/main/contracts/cloudlink/README.md): This directory is the only AetherEdge CloudLink contract surface. Schema IDs, file paths, MQTT topics, session establishment, delivery envelopes, ACKs, and replay requests have one canonical form and expose no protocol negotiation or…
- [Aether Data Processing JSON Schemas](https://github.com/EvanL1/AetherEdge/blob/main/contracts/data-processing/README.md): This directory publishes the single Draft 2020-12 transport schema family for Aether Data Processing.
- [Machine-readable contracts](https://github.com/EvanL1/AetherEdge/blob/main/contracts/README.md): This directory is reserved for stable configuration, command, event, and MCP schemas. Generated files must carry a generated header and are updated through the repository generation task rather than edited manually.
- [aether-acquisition-port](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/crates/aether-acquisition-port.md): Owner-only write capability for physical telemetry and status acquisition.
- [aether-application](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/crates/aether-application.md): Transport-neutral command and query use cases for the Aether edge kernel.
- [aether-cloudlink](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/crates/aether-cloudlink.md): Transport-neutral implementation of the experimental, digest-pinned public AetherContracts CloudLink subset. It provides strict closed JSON decoding, RFC 8785 business digests, session/epoch validation, stable delivery envelopes, Runtime…
- [aether-data-processing crate](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/crates/aether-data-processing.md): Strict, transport-neutral JSON codec for the Aether Data Processing processor boundary. It converts validated domain values to and from the fixed RFC 3339/JSON DTOs, encodes Aether-accepted DerivedData, and computes RFC 8785 input digests.
- [aether-dataplane](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/crates/aether-dataplane.md): aether-dataplane is Aether's business-neutral shared-memory core. It can be used by an embedded gateway without Redis, PostgreSQL, SQLx, routing models, or any HTTP stack.
- [aether-domain](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/crates/aether-domain.md): Industry-neutral, nostd domain types for the Aether edge kernel.
- [aether-integration-contract](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/crates/aether-integration-contract.md): Strict product-side Rust binding for the experimental AetherContracts aether.integration v1alpha1 contract in the 0.1.0-alpha.4 candidate.
- [aether-pack](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/crates/aether-pack.md): Industry-neutral domain-pack manifest loading for the Aether edge kernel. The crate validates a pack's own release identity, distribution identity, compatible Aether range, required capability and protocol IDs, explicitly uncommissioned…
- [aether-ports](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/crates/aether-ports.md): Small, object-safe capability interfaces for kernel and downstream adapters.
- [aether-edge-sdk](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/crates/aether-sdk.md): Versioned beta facade for embedding the Aether AI-native IoT edge kernel.
- [aether-testkit](https://docs.aetheriot.ai/crates/aether-testkit.md): Reusable conformance checks and deterministic test doubles for Aether adapter authors.
- [Core Crate Instructions](https://github.com/EvanL1/AetherEdge/blob/main/crates/AGENTS.md): These instructions apply to all crates in this directory.
